text:
Casey Cizikas got his 1,000th game on Saturday, a secondary assist on Ondrej Palat's second goal, and a late block on a Moritz Seider one-timer to help close out a 3-2 win in Detroit. It was a fitting night for a team that keeps finding ways. The Islanders are 11-6-5 with points in seven straight (4-0-3), and our playoff odds have them at 44%.

The way they're doing it deserves a closer look. New York has only 47% of the expected goals this season (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and even during the streak it was 48%. The difference is in net: the Islanders have allowed about 14 fewer goals than their chances against would predict, and Ilya Sorokin has been the reason lately, with a .928 save rate and 5.6 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. By our numbers they have about six more points than their play has earned.

The fun part is the kids. Matthew Schaefer has 15 points in his last 10 games, including his first career hat trick against Columbus, and his pair with Logan Stanley wins 55% of the expected goals at 5v5. Victor Eklund is drawing Calder attention, and Simon Holmstrom's seven-game point streak has given the Kyle Palmieri and Bo Horvat line (58% of expected goals) a real third threat.

What we'd watch: whether the shot share climbs before Sorokin cools, and the penalty count, at 4.09 penalties taken a game.
